newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian kangaroo debt market widens to HK.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian kangaroo debt market widens to HK.

text.p: Australia's budding kangaroo debt market widened its investment profile with the announcement that GE Capital Finance Ltd (Hong Kong) will be issuing a A$50 million three-year floating rate note under the structure.
This is the fourth kangaroo offering, which are debt instruments issued by foreign borrowers in the Australian domestic market, although until today issuance had been exclusively by Korean names.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA), which has been mandated to lead the new deal, said initial discussions with investors have been very positive.
CBA said that the notes will be priced at 18 basis points over bank bills and will be fully placed before its launch in late February.
"Australia investors are attracted by the positive spread on the notes and the protection against future rises in interest rates," CBA said in a statement.
It also said the success of a similar floating transaction for Korea Long term Credit Bank in mid-December last year had encouraged the bank to proceed with the deal.
CBA has been one of the main banks at the forefront of developing the kangaroo market.
Such debt raisings are seen partially filling the investment hole in Australia left by the reining back of debt issuance programmes of the Australian Treasury and state governments.
It is also hoped that this new market will raise the profile of Australia as an investment centre within the Asia region.
GE Capital Finance is wholly-owned by AAA/Aaa rated General Electric Capital Corporation (GECC), a familiar borrower in the Eurobond market.
GECC is wholly owned by General Electric Company USA. Last week two Thai banks, Thai Farmers Bank and Bangkok Bank were rumoured as potential issues in the market.
